title: Variance as a sum of squared Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite sets, and let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$ that assigns positive mass to every point. Suppose $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$ is an orthonormal basis of the complex-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle_p=\sum_{x\in\Omega}p(x)\overline{f(x)}g(x)$, and that $\phi_{i_0}$ is the constant-one function for a distinguished index $i_0\in I$. For any $f:\Omega\to\mathbb C$, its variance, defined as $\langle f-\mathbb E_p f,f-\mathbb E_p f\rangle_p$ with $\mathbb E_p f=\sum_xp(x)f(x)$, equals $\sum_{i\in I,\ i\ne i_0}|\widehat f(i)|^2$, where $\widehat f(i)$ is the coefficient of $\phi_i$ in the basis expansion of $f$.
